owner: akiendelllinux_cc_0 (CC) gates writes. Akien's call, 2026-07-26: 'we're going to add a new step to some workflows: demo. DEMO goes on tickets I wanna watch work.'
intention: A DEMO gate: a proof executed IN FRONT OF Akien, bound per-node at cast time on the work he wants to watch. Not a stage — a gate. It seals through the quorum door that already exists, with Akien as the reviewer and CC as the notary.
why: The founding reason Cairn was started over, in Akien's words: the prior system 'didn't have the proving structure there. and we didn't have me trying to be insistent on showing me each thing working.' DEMO is that second half made structural instead of remembered. It is also the honest answer to a failure this system has already shown twice in two sessions — a component reported complete because its internal work was complete, while the thing it exists to do was never connected (the quorum gate with nowhere to sign; inference_domain with no host). A green proof did not catch either. A human watching it work would have.
traces_to: Law 8 — nothing enters proven-space without a proof a hollow build couldn't pass. A demo is that proof with a witness; a hollow build survives a green suite far more easily than it survives being watched.
Law 3 — nothing is known until measured, and a demonstration is a measurement taken in the world rather than in the test harness.
telos — the founding intention of getting Akien out of RUNNING the system is not the same as getting him out of SEEING it. DEMO is deliberately his time spent, on the nodes he chooses.

gates.prove_gate: proof gate — the tester runs the proof and emits a VALIDATION.

falsifier: A node with DEMO bound cannot reach PROVED without a DEMO validation, and the append door must REFUSE the transition otherwise — not warn, refuse. The validation must carry Akien as the verdict-giver and a DIFFERENT hand as notary; quorum.seal() already refuses a notary who also reviewed, so a self-sealed demo is refused for free and that refusal must be proven, not assumed. A hollow build — a DEMO flag that records a boolean nobody signed, or a node that reaches PROVED with the flag set and no validation — fails.
horizon: Re-read after the first three demos. The open question deliberately not answered: what happens when a demo goes RED. It should kick back to build (CP2, the same disposition as a red proof) rather than being a veto, but no demo has been run and guessing the routing ahead of one is inventing physics for a case we have not seen.
distinctions_recorded: IT IS A GATE, NOT A STAGE — the ruling. A stage is where a node IS; a gate is what it must pass to move. Adding DEMO as a stage would mean editing every workflow path that could ever want it, and the emit-chokepoint would then refuse the paths that do not have it. As a gate it binds per-node with no path change at all, which is why it can be selective ('tickets I wanna watch work') without forking the class definitions.

PER-NODE OPT-IN IS THE GENUINELY NEW MECHANISM. Today a node's gate-set comes from its CLASS. DEMO is chosen at cast time for this node specifically. So what this actually builds is: a node may bind an EXTRA gate beyond its class's set. DEMO is the first user of that, and it will not be the last.

THE MACHINERY LANDED YESTERDAY AND THIS IS ITS SECOND TENANT. quorum.seal() (cairn fc6bfe2) already enforces distinct hands, refuses a signature carrying no `restated`, and records a red as a VERDICT that kicks back rather than an exception. validations_path_for_artifact gave a non-code artifact somewhere to be sealed. DEMO needs no new record shape — it is the same ratified eight fields through the same door.
dependencies: BUILDME needs the quorum door (BUILT, cairn fc6bfe2) and the emit-chokepoint (BUILT, cairn/tools/base/transitions.py). Nothing outstanding.
provenance: Akien, 2026-07-26, while setting the session's priority order: 'we're going to add a new step to some workflows: demo. DEMO goes on tickets I wanna watch work. Librarian chat will have DEMO on it. maybe it's just a kind of validation or sign off by me. i dunno.' CC's read — gate not stage, per-node opt-in, rides the quorum door — was offered in the same exchange and is what is cast here; the uncertainty Akien flagged ('i dunno') is resolved into the horizon question above rather than silently settled.
filed_edges: LIBRARIAN CHAT IS THE NAMED FIRST RIDER — Akien called it out by name. It cannot bind the gate until it is itself cast, so the binding happens at that node's cast, not here.

WHAT COUNTS AS 'WATCHING IT WORK' is not specified and deliberately so. A live screen-share, a recorded run, a session transcript — no evidence yet says which, and the first three demos will say more than a ruling made now.

[RESOLVED 2026-08-20] WHO BINDS IT: Akien, at /sorted — he picks which tickets carry DEMO. WHAT CLEARS IT: Akien watches it run. The quorum door seals it with him as reviewer and CC as notary. No ceremony beyond the existing quorum shape.
